clue.text: Stop in unoccupied zone when cleared

indicators.note: a word cleared of its contents keeps only its outside letters, the middle emptied out

parts.note: the word zone with its middle letters removed

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt in an empty area once it has been cleared, like traffic or security directions.
explanation.walkthrough: FREE plus ZE gives FREEZE; 'in' and 'when' only join the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze is to stop moving entirely, as in the command to halt on the spot.

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being toyed with and moved about into new order

explanation.surface: A musical note: the key in which a triangle part is being played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks musical, sitting beside an instrument, but it is the adjective meaning essential.
explanation.definitionFit: Something key is essential or central, and an integral part is one that cannot be removed.

clue.text: Not a mile away from Havana?

definitions.text: Not a mile away from Havana?

parts.note: surface reading: very near, nearly reaching something
setter's reading: near to, yet failing to be, a Cuban smoke, since a Havana is a type of cigar

explanation.surface: Seems to be describing a place a short distance from the Cuban capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A Havana is a Cuban cigar; the phrase meaning a near miss literally says near, but not a cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an attempt that came very near success without quite achieving it, fitting 'not a mile away'.

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
ticker is informal slang for the heart

explanation.surface: A tiny label in the shape of a heart, like a gift tag.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticker is an adhesive label, so it serves as a tag attached to something.

clue.text: Using one of two bent objects, come what may

definitions.text: Using one of two bent objects
definitions.meaning: cryptic meaning: by means of either a hook or a crook, both curved implements
second meaning: by any means necessary, whatever happens

explanation.surface: Using a curved tool to get something done regardless of obstacles.
explanation.walkthrough: A crook is a shepherd's hooked staff, so both hook and crook are bent objects.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means achieving something by whatever means possible, fair or foul, much like 'come what may'.

clue.text: Basket's opening, draw out of it

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, where it begins

parts.note: a lotto is a lottery, decided by a draw

explanation.surface: Pulling something out of a basket that has just been opened, like a prize draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of it' looks like part of the drawing action, but it is the definition: helplessly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely drunk, and someone out of it is too intoxicated to function.

indicators.note: something oxygenated has oxygen put into it, so the symbol goes inside

parts.note: cl is the abbreviation for centilitre
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A recipe step: a measure of fizzy liquid poured to make a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cola is a sweet carbonated soft drink, flavoured originally with kola nut.

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: nori is the edible seaweed used to wrap sushi

explanation.surface: A dietary mineral contained in seaweed that someone refused to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Seaweed really is rich in this mineral, so the surface is almost true.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron is a metallic element, counted among the dietary minerals the body needs.

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like praise for some books; the words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit means illuminated, hence brilliant, and is also a common abbreviation for literature, the body of written works.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the hue of a lemon or a canary

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a pale shade, the opposite of a bold one.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is informal for cowardly, the opposite of brave, and is also a primary colour.

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end of the preceding word, its final letter

parts.note: evens is a betting price, one kind of odds

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which numbers end up being odd.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: sevens are numbers that are odd, while the wordplay finds a betting term after the last letter of 'Numbers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is an odd number, so its plural names a set of odd numbers, matching the whole clue.

clue.text: A trio unfortunately locked in jail, European

indicators.note: something locked in is shut inside something else, enclosed by it

parts.note: the can is slang for prison

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters end up in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Three people regrettably imprisoned, one of them from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Croatian is a native of Croatia, a country in south-east Europe.

indicators.note: after places the word it follows second, so the clue's later part is written first

parts.note: house is another name for bingo, called out on a full card

explanation.surface: Playing bingo to cheer up after a bad time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the bingo word second. Heartbreak House is a play by George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's Heartbreak House is a stage drama of 1919, so the title is an instance of a play.

indicators.note: has means holds within, so the run of letters is held inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: Noticing that someone's nose clearly has a pimple on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a blemish on the nose, but it is the verb meaning notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or catch sight of it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

indicators.note: something knotted is twisted and tangled, so the letters are tied into a new order

explanation.surface: A tie that has been knotted and then trimmed short.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate someone is to separate them from others, the same sense as cutting them off.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the fluid that circulates in a plant
second meaning: to weaken or exhaust gradually

explanation.surface: Some important fluid sitting in a drainpipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drain' reads as a noun, a pipe, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sap is the life-giving fluid of plants, and to sap strength is to drain it away.

clue.text: Belter, teaspoon on boiled egg, possibly?

definitions.meaning: cryptic meaning: a spoon tapping an egg breaks its shell

explanation.surface: A hard whack of a teaspoon on a breakfast egg.
explanation.walkthrough: A belter is British slang for something excellent; the second part playfully names a thing that breaks a shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cracker is informal for an excellent example, and literally a teaspoon striking a shell is what breaks it open.

clue.text: Food made without stuffing, popular takeaway dish

indicators.note: a word without its stuffing has lost its inner filling, leaving just the outer letters

parts.note: the word made with its middle removed

explanation.surface: Food cooked without any filling, a well-liked thing to order out.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow mein is a Chinese dish of fried noodles, a staple of takeaway menus.

clue.text: As is jargon-busting prior to a card game

indicators.note: busting means bursting into the middle of something, so one piece breaks in

parts.note: cant is the specialised jargon of a group

explanation.surface: Plain speaking cutting through jargon before a game of cards begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-type card game played with two packs, popular in the mid twentieth century.

clue.text: Love and personality represented in book of letters

indicators.note: represented means presented afresh in another form, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Romance and character portrayed in a story told through correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistolary novel tells its story through a series of letters or documents exchanged by characters.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cadge off others
second meaning: a light airy sweet bake

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like begging for a slice; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to live off others' generosity, and a sponge is also a light cake made with eggs.

clue.text: Bug for example's eaten raw, I gathered

indicators.note: something eaten is taken inside, so the outer piece swallows the other

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: gathered material is bunched and pleated, so the letters are folded into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone noticed an insect, for instance, being eaten uncooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I gathered' looks like 'I understood', but 'gathered' acts on the letters of raw and I.
explanation.definitionFit: An earwig is an insect with pincers, and bug is a loose everyday word for any insect.

clue.text: Meal is on after whipping up kind of pudding

indicators.note: whipping up means beating and mixing, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Dinner is served after a dessert has been whisked together.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is coarse wheat flour, cooked with milk into a traditional British school dessert.

indicators.note: something bitten by another is held in its jaws, so the letters sit inside the words

parts.note: the letters span the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: An indignant claim that a woodpecker would never peck another bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a large bird of prey, and a crossword staple.

parts.note: re means concerning or on the subject of
a smut is a sooty mark or smudge

explanation.surface: Having a comment to make about indecent material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smut' suggests filth in talk, but here it is literal soot, a dirty mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a brief comment, quite literally something one says.

clue.text: Gem in a newly closed book

indicators.note: newly means done over afresh, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A jewel found inside a book that has just been shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closed book' looks like a literal book shut on a gem, but it is the idiom for something baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed book is an idiom for something or someone impossible to understand, which is what a mystery is.

clue.text: Three without one … leads to this?

definitions.text: Three without one … leads to this?

indicators.note: leads are what go at the front, so each word supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: A simple sum: take one away from three and see what you get.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: three minus one is the answer, and so are the first letters of the opening three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtracting a single unit from three leaves the number between one and three.

indicators.note: something cut has had its end trimmed off, losing its final letter

parts.note: Cork is a county and city in Ireland, so its people are this, as an example

explanation.surface: A bloom picked from County Cork, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cork' is not the bark but the Irish county; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a garden plant with showy sword-leaved blooms, named after the Greek goddess of the rainbow.
